title: Academy Foundation Readiness Check
description: A small interdisciplinary demonstration of the universal assessment engine.
subject: interdisciplinary

items.prompt: A course contains 36 weeks divided evenly into 12 units. How many weeks are assigned to each unit?

options.label: 2 weeks
3 weeks
4 weeks
6 weeks

feedback.correct: Correct. Dividing 36 by 12 gives 3 weeks per unit.
feedback.incorrect: Review equal-group division: total weeks divided by total units.

items.prompt: A student earned 42 points out of 50. Enter the percentage score.

feedback.incorrect: Divide the earned points by possible points, then multiply by 100.

items.prompt: Which evidence most directly supports the claim that a substance underwent a chemical change?

options.label: It was cut into smaller pieces.
It changed from a solid to a liquid.
A new gas formed during the reaction.
Its container was moved to another table.

feedback.correct: Correct. Formation of a new gas can be evidence that new substances formed.
feedback.incorrect: Distinguish a physical change in form or state from evidence of new substances.

items.prompt: Which statement is the strongest evidence-based conclusion?

options.label: The program is perfect because one student liked it.
The program may be effective because scores improved across three measured groups.
The program must be ineffective because it requires effort.
No conclusion is possible whenever people disagree.

feedback.correct: Correct. The statement is cautious and tied to evidence from multiple measured groups.
feedback.incorrect: Look for a conclusion that matches the strength and limits of the available evidence.

items.prompt: A civic proposal affects several communities differently. What should an evidence-based review do first?

options.label: Ignore groups with smaller populations.
Measure likely benefits, burdens, rights, and implementation effects.
Choose the most emotional argument.
Assume every community will experience the same result.

feedback.correct: Correct. Responsible civic analysis examines evidence, rights, tradeoffs, and implementation.
feedback.incorrect: A public decision should be evaluated across affected groups and measurable consequences.

items.prompt: Select every responsible practice when using an online research source.

options.label: Check the author or institution.
Check the publication or update date.
Inspect the evidence and cited sources.
Trust the first result without comparison.

feedback.correct: Correct. Authorship, date, evidence, and comparison all support responsible source evaluation.
feedback.partial: Some responsible practices were selected, but the set is incomplete or includes an unsafe shortcut.
feedback.incorrect: Search ranking alone does not establish credibility.

items.prompt: I prefer to see an example before attempting a new kind of problem independently.

feedback.exploratory: This preference is temporary and revisable. It may guide practice format but will not restrict your opportunities.

items.prompt: Describe one academic skill you want to strengthen and one kind of evidence that would show improvement.

feedback.manual-review: Your response was saved for teacher or mentor review. It should name a skill and a measurable form of evidence.
